entities.summary: Telauges was a Samian Pythagorean philosopher and, according to tradition, the son of Pythagoras and Theano. Born in Samos, a Greek city-state in the 6th century BCE, Telauges was educated in the philosophical and mathematical traditions of his father and other prominent Pythagoreans. He is believed to have traveled extensively throughout the ancient world, including to Egypt and Babylon, where he may have studied with prominent scholars. Telauges' philosophical views are not well-documented, but he is thought to have been influenced by the Pythagorean emphasis on the interconnectedness of all things and the importance of living in harmony with nature. His teachings likely played a significant role in shaping the philosophical traditions of the ancient Mediterranean world. Telauges' legacy can be seen in the philosophical schools of his time, which continued to influence Western philosophy for centuries to come. As a key figure in the development of Pythagoreanism, Telauges' ideas on the nature of reality, the universe, and human existence remain relevant today.
